en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Kumāribhūtavagga 74.
The Training Rule on Being Less Than Twelve Years Old.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns who were less than twelve years [of standing] were giving the full admission.
They were foolish and incompetent, not knowing what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Their co-resident pupils were also foolish and incompetent.
They do not know what is allowable or what is unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who are of few desires... [as above]... were indignant, disparaged [this], and complained, saying:
"How indeed can bhikkhunīs give the full admission to those who are less than twelve years [of standing]?"... [as above]...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are giving the full admission to those who are less than twelve years [of standing]?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can nuns who are less than twelve years [of standing] give the full admission?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule: [The training rule follows]"
“Whatever nun, however, who is less than twelve years [of standing] should give the full admission, it is an offense of expiation.
Regarding “whatever nun”: whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ... [as before] ...
this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Less than twelve years" means:
"Less than twelve years old.
"Should ordain" means: should confer full admission (upasampadā).
If she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, thinking, “I will give the full admission,” or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For each of the two formal proclamations (kammavācā), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal act (*kammavācā*), there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) for the community and for the teacher.
There is no offense—
If she ordains one who is fully twelve years old;
if she is insane;
if she is a first-offender.
The fourth training rule is finished.
